video.title: How I Use Web Scraping to Find Products That Sell for 20x the Price

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates how to use the Oxylabs web scraper API (his sponsor) to scrape Amazon best-seller lists in three categories (pet accessories, household/health, children's education books), then analyse them in Google Sheets and Claude to find products with strong sales rank but low review counts. He then finds near-identical products on Alibaba via image search and works through landed-cost and Amazon fee maths (about 30% net margin claimed on a cat feeder). He adds extra screening tactics: one-star test, fee-tier size shrinking, variations, rating distribution, Google Trends, Amazon Choice badges. Key takeaway: pick Amazon products by data (rank vs review mismatch) rather than personal interest, but the margin maths is rough and the evidence is promotional.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; says he has imported from Alibaba/AliExpress for 17 years; Oxylabs sponsor affiliate

ideas.name: Amazon FBA product arbitrage using scraped best-seller data (Alibaba sourcing)
ideas.one_liner: Scrape Amazon best-seller lists, find products with high sales rank but few reviews, source a near-identical item from Alibaba and sell it via FBA.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales on Amazon; margin between Alibaba landed cost and Amazon price less FBA fees
ideas.customer: Amazon shoppers in the chosen marketplace (US .com in the demo)
ideas.problem: Most Amazon sellers pick products by personal interest rather than data, so they enter saturated or low-margin niches.
ideas.offer: A copy or slightly improved version of an under-reviewed best-selling product (e.g. a bundled gravity-fed cat feeder and water dispenser), differentiated by colour, material or size.

pricing.model: Match competitor price on Amazon, or slightly under

price_points.label: Stainless paper towel holder Amazon price

pricing.notes: Leave extra margin for Amazon ads

acquisition_channels.details: Amazon search ranking; seller aims to take the position of a product with few reviews. First listing image is stressed as critical; use lifestyle photos not Alibaba stock photos. Fewer returns boost ranking. Amazon ads suggested.

quote.text: I cannot emphasize enough how important that first image is on your Amazon listing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Order about 100 units from an Alibaba supplier and ship directly to an Amazon warehouse; Amazon FBA handles storage, fulfilment and shipping to the consumer.
unit_economics_claims: Cat feeder: Alibaba about $1.50-2 per unit, shipping and tariffs about $5, landed about $7
Amazon fees $10-15 (large bulky); total cost $16-21; net profit about $9 per unit at $30, about 30% margin
Shrinking the product to drop a fee tier could save about $3 per unit
Paper towel holder sources at $0.40-1.77 and sells for $5
ideas.startup_cost: About $155 for a first 100-unit order of the cat feeder (excluding shipping, tariffs, FBA fees and ads)

acquisition.how: Amazon marketplace search and ads are inbound and automatable; listing creation, images and ad tuning can be agent-assisted but need checks.

onboarding.how: No customer onboarding; Amazon handles the buyer relationship.

delivery.how: Physical goods: sourcing, samples, supplier negotiation, QC and freight need a human, though FBA handles last-mile fulfilment. Research and scraping can be agent-run.

billing.how: Amazon collects payment and pays out automatically.

support.how: Amazon handles most customer service and returns; the seller occasionally handles reviews, Q&A and supplier issues.

uk_applicability.notes: Amazon.co.uk and FBA UK exist, and the scraper supports other domains. Differences: UK VAT, import duties and customs, UKCA/CE product safety rules, different FBA fee tiers, and the tariff figure quoted is US-specific.

risks: Trademark and copyright infringement, especially on branded books from China
Low margins could be wiped out by fees, ads and returns
New unvetted Alibaba suppliers and quality control issues
Review-rate maths is a rough estimate
Scraping may breach Amazon terms of service
Competitors may copy again; tariffs may change

ideas.name: Imported children's books and workbooks sold on Amazon
ideas.one_liner: Source generic kids' workbooks and books cheaply from Alibaba and sell them on Amazon using proven title structures.
ideas.customer: Parents of young children buying education and learning books
ideas.problem: Demand for learning books is steady, and books are cheap to ship because they are small and light.
ideas.offer: Generic kindergarten workbooks, coloring books and similar titles with 'what it is, what it does, who it's for' titles.

pricing.notes: A 33-book Oxford Reading Tree set shown at $167 on Amazon vs $12 on Alibaba, but trademark risk

acquisition_channels.details: Amazon search; titles follow 'what it is, what it does, who it's for', lead with quantity, age-gate, and use 'learn to' prefixes.

ideas.delivery: Import from Alibaba and ship to FBA.
unit_economics_claims: Workbook about $0.80 on Alibaba vs about $7 on Amazon

acquisition.how: Amazon listing optimisation and ads are mostly automatable.

uk_applicability.notes: Works via Amazon.co.uk, but books have no import VAT issues like other goods, though copyright and children's product safety rules apply. UK import duty/VAT apply to books differently.

risks: Low price may mean thin margins

tactics.name: Rank vs review-count mismatch screen
steps: Scrape Amazon best sellers for a category using its browse node ID (Claude can supply the IDs)
Export JSON, convert to CSV with Claude, paste into Google Sheets
Add a column dividing ratings count by best-seller rank and sort
Apply conditional formatting colour scale to the rating count to find outliers near the top ranks
Ignore items with high rank and thousands of reviews (saturated); target high rank with under about 300 reviews

quote.text: If a product has a very good or highseller rank, but a low review count of like under 300
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use Claude to analyse screenshots of top candidates
steps: Screenshot the listings and the sheet
Run two separate prompts: one with your hypothesis and one unbiased
Compare what features differentiate (bundle, simplicity, price)
Ask for improvement angles like better materials

tactics.name: Alibaba image search sourcing and landed cost
steps: Save the Amazon product image and run Alibaba image search
Or scrape Alibaba with Oxylabs using a search term and sort by price and MOQ
Compare MOQ, supplier years in business
Estimate sea freight and tariffs about $4-5 per unit
Ship directly to Amazon warehouse
Check FBA fees and size tier

tactics.name: Tangential category piggybacking
steps: If a category is dominated by big brands, scrape an adjacent accessory category (e.g. paper towel holders)
Apply the same rank/review screen
Source the accessory from Alibaba

tactics.name: One-star test and variation mining
steps: Count one-star reviews by complaint type
If about 40% cite the same problem, fix it and sell at the same price
Scrape Q&A and reviews for phrases like 'I wish'
Ask supplier for colours, sizes or bundles requested

tactics.name: Fee-tier size optimisation
steps: Check Amazon size and weight thresholds
Shrink product slightly to fall into a lower fee tier
Optionally lower price to lift conversion

tactics.name: Trend and badge checks
steps: Check Google Trends for the keyword over 5 years
Accept seasonal products if trend is up
Look for categories with multiple Amazon Choice badges as sign of no category leader
Check rating distribution shape: mostly 5-star plus few 1-star suggests fixable defect

lessons.lesson: Choose products by data (demand versus competition signals) rather than personal interest.

lessons.lesson: A saturated-looking category can still have gaps; look at demand vs supply signals and adjacent categories.
Small physical tweaks (size, weight, bundle, colour) can improve margin or conversion without a new product.
Simple products with fewer features tend to have fewer returns, which Amazon's algorithm rewards.
Use AI to speed up analysis and spot things the operator overlooks, but test with both biased and unbiased prompts.
Seasonal businesses can still be very profitable if planned for.

quote.text: Seasonal is great. It's easy to plan for.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do the landed-cost and fee maths before ordering stock; margins decide viability.
Listing quality (first image, real-life photos) differentiates copy products from lazy stock-photo sellers.
Test suppliers and demand with a small first order (about 100 units) before scaling.

evidence_quality.rationale: The method is demonstrated live with real scraped data, but the profit figures are rough estimates, not results from the host's own Amazon business; no first-hand FBA performance numbers are given. The video is partly promotional.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsored by Oxylabs (the host promotes an affiliate link and promo code); also links to his other videos and free spreadsheet.
